messages.content: Write `countSpaces(s)` — count space characters.

<think>
Iterate each character, count those equal to a space using === text comparison.
</think>
```falcon
func countSpaces(s) = {
    local count = 0
    for (i: 1 .. s.textLen()) {
        if (s.segment(i, 1) === " ") { count = count + 1 }
    }
    count
}
println(countSpaces("hello world"))
println(countSpaces("  two  spaces  "))
println(countSpaces("nospaces"))
```
Write `longestWordStartingWith(sentence, ch)` — longest word starting with given char.

<think>
Split sentence into words, filter those starting with ch, then find the longest by textLen().
</think>
```falcon
func longestWordStartingWith(sentence, ch) = {
    local words = sentence.splitAtSpaces().filter { w -> w.startsWith(ch) }
    if (words ? emptyList) {
        ""
    } else {
        words.max { a, b -> a.textLen() > b.textLen() }
    }
}
println(longestWordStartingWith("the big brown bear broke branches", "b"))
println(longestWordStartingWith("hello world", "z"))
```
Write `toPhoneFormat(digits)` — formats `"1234567890"` as `"(123) 456-7890"`.

<think>
Extract segments of the digit string using segment(): area code (1-3), exchange (4-6), number (7-10). Assemble with formatting characters.
</think>
```falcon
func toPhoneFormat(digits) = {
    local area = digits.segment(1, 3)
    local exchange = digits.segment(4, 3)
    local number = digits.segment(7, 4)
    "(" _ area _ ") " _ exchange _ "-" _ number
}
println(toPhoneFormat("1234567890"))
```

Write `chunk(list, n)` that splits a list into groups of n. Test `([1..9], 3)`.

<think>
Slide through the list in steps of n, slicing each group. The last group may be smaller.
</think>
```falcon
func chunk(list, n) = {
    local result = []
    local i = 1
    while (i <= list.listLen()) {
        local end = min(i + n - 1, list.listLen())
        result.add(list.slice(i, end))
        i = i + n
    }
    result
}
local nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9]
println(chunk(nums, 3))
println(chunk(nums, 4))
```

Write `matMul(a, b)` for 2x2 matrix multiplication.

<think>
Matrix multiply 2x2: result[i][j] = sum over k of a[i][k]*b[k][j]. 1-based indexing in Falcon.
Store matrices as lists of rows, each row a list. result[1][1]=a[1][1]*b[1][1]+a[1][2]*b[2][1].
</think>
```falcon
func matMul(a, b) = {
    local r00 = a[1][1]*b[1][1] + a[1][2]*b[2][1]
    local r01 = a[1][1]*b[1][2] + a[1][2]*b[2][2]
    local r10 = a[2][1]*b[1][1] + a[2][2]*b[2][1]
    local r11 = a[2][1]*b[1][2] + a[2][2]*b[2][2]
    [[r00, r01], [r10, r11]]
}
```

Write `mergeAlternating(a, b)` — interleave two lists. Test.

<think>
Take elements from a and b alternately. When one is exhausted, append the rest of the other.
</think>
```falcon
func mergeAlternating(a, b) = {
    local result = []
    local i = 1
    while (i <= a.listLen() || i <= b.listLen()) {
        if (i <= a.listLen()) { result.add(a[i]) }
        if (i <= b.listLen()) { result.add(b[i]) }
        i = i + 1
    }
    result
}
```

Write `longestIncreasingSubsequence(list)` — return its length. Test `[3,1,4,1,5,9,2,6]`.

<think>
LIS using patience-sorting DP: maintain tails[] where tails[i] is the smallest tail of all increasing subsequences of length i+1.
For each element, binary search in tails for first value >= element. Replace or extend.
Falcon: implement binary search manually (no break, use flag+exit pattern). 1-based indexing.
</think>
```falcon
func lisLength(list) = {
    local tails = []
    for (x in list) {
        local lo = 1
        local hi = tails.listLen()
        local pos = tails.listLen() + 1
        while (lo <= hi) {
            local mid = floor((lo + hi) / 2)
            if (tails[mid] < x) {
                lo = mid + 1
            } else {
                pos = mid
                hi = mid - 1
            }
        }
        if (pos > tails.listLen()) {
            tails.add(x)
        } else {
            tails[pos] = x
        }
    }
    tails.listLen()
}
println(lisLength([3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]))
println(lisLength([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]))
println(lisLength([5, 4, 3, 2, 1]))
```
Write `majorityElement(list)` — element appearing more than n/2 times. Test.

<think>
Boyer-Moore voting: maintain a candidate and count. If count is 0, switch candidate. Candidate is the majority.
</think>
```falcon
func majorityElement(list) = {
    local candidate = list[1]
    local count = 1
    for (i: 2 .. list.listLen()) {
        if (count == 0) {
            candidate = list[i]
            count = 1
        } else if (list[i] == candidate) {
            count = count + 1
        } else {
            count = count - 1
        }
    }
    candidate
}
println(majorityElement([2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2]))
println(majorityElement([3, 3, 4, 2, 3, 3, 3]))
```
Write a simple matrix addition for two 2x2 matrices represented as `[[a,b],[c,d]]`.

<think>
Element-wise addition of two matrices. Add corresponding elements row by row.
</think>
```falcon
func matAdd(a, b) = {
    local result = []
    for (i: 1 .. a.listLen()) {
        local row = []
        for (j: 1 .. a[i].listLen()) {
            row.add(a[i][j] + b[i][j])
        }
        result.add(row)
    }
    result
}
```

Write `rotateMatrix90(matrix)` — rotate 3x3 clockwise. Test.

<think>
Clockwise 90° rotation: new[i][j] = old[n-j+1][i]. Build new matrix by transposing and reversing rows.
</think>
```falcon
func rotateMatrix90(m) = {
    local n = m.listLen()
    local result = []
    for (i: 1 .. n) {
        local row = []
        for (j: 1 .. n) {
            row.add(m[n - j + 1][i])
        }
        result.add(row)
    }
    result
}
```

Write `shuffle(list)` — pseudo-random reorder using randInt swaps. Test.

<think>
Fisher-Yates shuffle: for each position from end to 2, swap with a random earlier position.
</think>
```falcon
func shuffle(list) = {
    local result = copyList(list)
    local n = result.listLen()
    for (i: n .. 2 step -1) {
        local j = randInt(1, i)
        local tmp = result[i]
        result[i] = result[j]
        result[j] = tmp
    }
    result
}
println(shuffle([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]))
```

Write `applyToOddIndices(list, fn)`.

Write `interquartileRange(list)` — Q3 - Q1. Test.

<think>
Sort the list, Q1 is median of lower half, Q3 is median of upper half. IQR = Q3 - Q1.
</think>
```falcon
func median(list) = {
    local n = list.listLen()
    if (n % 2 == 1) {
        list[floor(n / 2) + 1]
    } else {
        (list[n / 2] + list[n / 2 + 1]) / 2
    }
}

func iqr(list) = {
    local sorted = list.sort { a, b -> a < b }
    local n = sorted.listLen()
    local lower = sorted.slice(1, floor(n / 2))
    local upper = sorted.slice(floor(n / 2) + 1, n)
    median(upper) - median(lower)
}
println(iqr([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]))
```

Write `subdict(d, from, to)` — return entries within alphabetical key range. Test.

<think>
Filter pairs where key >= from and key <= to lexicographically, build new dict.

Write `mergeLists(a, b, key)` — merge list of dicts on common key. Test.

<think>
Build index from b keyed by the merge key. For each dict in a, merge with matching dict from b.
</think>
```falcon
func mergeLists(a, b, key) = {
    local index = {}
    for (item in b) { index.set(item.get(key,""), item) }
```

```falcon
func colorFromHSV(h, s, v) = {
    local c = v * s
    local x = c * (1 - abs(mod(h / 60, 2) - 1))
    local m = v - c
    local r = 0
    local g = 0
    local b = 0
    if (h < 60) { r = c  g = x  b = 0 }
    else if (h < 120) { r = x  g = c  b = 0 }
    else if (h < 180) { r = 0  g = c  b = x }
    else if (h < 240) { r = 0  g = x  b = c }
    else if (h < 300) { r = x  g = 0  b = c }
    else { r = c  g = 0  b = x }
    makeColor([floor((r+m)*255), floor((g+m)*255), floor((b+m)*255)])
}
```
